exploiting_exit_rate_per_hour.meaning: exit rate per hour achieved by a user exploiting frequent small redemptions (redemptions every 5 minutes), as reported
exploiting_exit_rate_per_hour.checkpoint: after exploit redemptions over one hour

regular_exit_rate_per_hour.meaning: exit rate per hour for regular users making single redemptions, as reported
regular_exit_rate_per_hour.checkpoint: after regular single redemption over one hour

speed_advantage_factor.meaning: reported 2.8x speed advantage of exploiting users over regular users

assumptions: The report's safety intent is that splitting redemptions across multiple transactions must not yield a higher exit rate than a single redemption.
Exit rates are compared over the same one-hour window.

unresolved.description: The report states exit-rate outcomes (30-40% vs 71% per hour) but does not provide a numeric cap formula or per-transaction redemption amounts, so the proportional relation cannot be fully bound to cap operands.
No explicit precondition statement establishes the pre-existing ETWAP market size or last-transaction timestamp before the exploit action.

limitations: The plan formalizes only the speed_advantage impact; other impacts are handled in separate passes.
The condition uses a truth predicate on an int symbol, which is a schema violation; this plan is returned as a candidate and may require correction.
